record.question:
A document service hosts its frontend behind CloudFront, accepts PDF uploads directly to S3, and submits asynchronous OCR jobs through a Regional API Gateway REST API. Processing and storage must remain in us-east-1. Users in Asia and the Middle East experience slow uploads and job-submission responses. Tests show that S3 Transfer Acceleration and an edge-optimized API endpoint improve those two paths enough to meet the targets at acceptable incremental cost. Backend processing time is already acceptable.

Which changes should the company make? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration and update upload requests or presigned upload URLs to use the supported acceleration endpoint.
Replace DynamoDB job metadata with Aurora Serverless and route database connections through RDS Proxy.
Introduce EC2 upload servers behind Global Accelerator, then copy uploaded PDFs from their EBS volumes into S3.
Deploy complete processing stacks and data copies in additional Regions and route users to regional deployments.
Change the REST API from a Regional endpoint to an edge-optimized endpoint, updating the deployment, custom-domain mapping, and DNS as required.

explanation.text:
<<1>> and <<5>> are correct. They address the two measured client paths while retaining the single-Region backend. Transfer Acceleration carries supported S3 transfers through AWS edge infrastructure, and an edge-optimized REST API uses a managed CloudFront distribution for API entry.

<<2>> changes a metadata store that is not the bottleneck.

<<3>> adds upload-server operation and another data-copy step when the tested managed S3 path meets the requirement.

<<4>> violates the stated single-Region processing and storage constraint.

The existing frontend distribution does not automatically accelerate separate direct-to-S3 uploads or calls to the Regional API hostname. Measure the actual client paths: acceleration benefits vary with location, network, and object size. An edge endpoint does not relocate the OCR execution or remove its regional processing time.

Official AWS references (checked September 18, 2026): [S3 acceleration measurement](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/transfer-acceleration-speed-comparison.html). [API Gateway edge entry](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/serverless-applications-lens/amazon-api-gateway.html). [Changing REST API endpoint types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-api-migration.html).

diagram_alt: Large uploads and small API submissions use different accelerated entry paths without moving backend processing to another Region.

sources.supports: Compare accelerated and ordinary multipart upload paths
Edge-optimized APIs use a managed CloudFront distribution
Regional and edge-optimized REST endpoints can be migrated with configuration and deployment updates

editorial_notes: Preserved answers 1 and 5. Replaced unsupported universal speed percentages and cost claims with measured benefit and a single-Region requirement.
